project.title: Little Red Riding Hood
project.description: A short fairy-tale production about a compassionate girl whose journey through a shadowed forest becomes a lesson in caution, courage, and the consequences of trusting a charming stranger.

world.name: The Forest Road
world.description: A close-knit rural community borders an ancient forest where familiar paths can quickly feel uncertain. Warm kitchens, a lonely cottage, and the dark trees form a world in which ordinary kindness must be balanced with good judgment.
world.timeline: The story unfolds over one autumn day, from a clear morning departure to an evening return home.
world.rules: The world is grounded in fairy-tale realism. Animals may speak, but people otherwise live by ordinary physical rules. Promises matter, the forest rewards attention, and strangers may conceal dangerous intentions behind polite words.
world.themes: Compassion guided by caution; the difference between politeness and trust; listening to intuition; community protection; learning without losing kindness.
world.geography: Little Red Riding Hood's home and her grandmother's cottage are connected by a narrow public road that passes through a dense old-growth forest. A woodcutter's trail crosses the road near the cottage.
world.references: A family-friendly adaptation of the European folktale, designed with storybook autumn colors, deep forest shadows, tactile handmade props, and restrained suspense rather than graphic violence.

characters.name: Little Red Riding Hood
characters.description: A thoughtful village girl who carries a basket of food to her ill grandmother. Her generosity begins the journey, her careful observations expose the wolf's disguise, and her mistake in revealing her destination teaches her to combine openness with discernment.
characters.appearance: A small, alert girl in a vivid red hooded cloak over a cream blouse, dark skirt, sturdy walking shoes, and a woven basket looped over one arm.
characters.personality: Kind, curious, observant, responsible, and initially too willing to assume that a friendly manner means a trustworthy heart.
characters.motivation: Deliver nourishing food to her sick grandmother before the day grows late.
characters.backstory: She has walked the forest road with adults many times and knows the route, but this is her first trip carrying responsibility on her own.
characters.voice_profile: Clear, youthful, and sincere. Her speech begins warm and unguarded, tightens as suspicion grows, and becomes calm and reflective after the rescue.

characters.name: Grandmother
characters.description: Little Red Riding Hood's recovering grandmother, whose quiet cottage is the destination of the journey. Though physically weak from illness, she remains composed, practical, and reassuring after the danger passes.
characters.appearance: A silver-haired woman with kind eyes, a pale linen nightcap, a knitted shawl, and a face made tired but not diminished by illness.
characters.motivation: Recover her strength and keep her granddaughter safe.
characters.backstory: She has lived beside the forest for many years and understands both its beauty and its risks.
characters.voice_profile: Soft, textured, and deliberate, with warmth beneath a trace of fatigue.

characters.name: The Wolf
characters.description: A clever forest predator who masks his intentions with courtly conversation. After learning where Little Red Riding Hood is headed, he races ahead, traps Grandmother, steals her clothes, and waits for the basket to arrive.
characters.appearance: A large gray humanoid, bi-pedal wolf with silver-tipped fur, amber eyes, long ears, powerful paws, and an expressive face that can shift from charming to threatening in an instant.
characters.personality: Patient, manipulative, theatrical, opportunistic, and quick to anger when his disguise fails.
characters.motivation: Steal the basket of food without having to chase or bargain for it.
characters.backstory: He has learned that travelers reveal more than they intend when he approaches them politely.
characters.voice_profile: Smooth and measured on the road; strained and falsely delicate in disguise; low, sharp, and feral when exposed.

characters.name: The Woodsman
characters.description: A local guardian who knows the forest trails and responds when he hears the struggle inside the cottage. He places himself between the wolf and the family, drives the animal away, and escorts Little Red Riding Hood safely home.
characters.appearance: A broad-shouldered worker in a weathered green coat, heavy boots, leather gloves, and a wool cap, carrying a well-used wood axe as a tool of his trade.
characters.personality: Steady, attentive, brave, restrained, and protective without being boastful.
characters.motivation: Protect his neighbors and keep the forest road safe.
characters.backstory: Years of working in the forest have taught him to recognize the sounds of ordinary wildlife and the sounds of trouble.
characters.voice_profile: Grounded, economical, and reassuring, with a firm command voice when confronting danger.

locations.name: Little Red Riding Hood's Home
locations.description: A modest stone-and-timber village house with a bright kitchen, shelves of preserves, a scarred preparation table, and an inviting hearth.
locations.geography: At the eastern edge of the village, near the entrance to the forest road.
locations.mood: Warm, orderly, secure, and gently bustling in the morning; quiet and reflective at night.

locations.name: The Dark Forest Road
locations.description: A narrow dirt road winding beneath tall pines and ancient oaks. Ferns crowd the edges, shafts of light divide the shadows, and fallen leaves.
locations.geography: Between the village and Grandmother's clearing, crossed by smaller animal tracks and a woodcutter's trail.
locations.mood: Beautiful but watchful, with mounting unease as the trees close around the road.

locations.name: Grandmother's Cottage
locations.description: A small cottage in a forest clearing, with a herb garden, low windows, a creaking front door, a pantry with a sturdy latch, and a bedroom warmed by a patchwork quilt and a small iron stove.
locations.geography: At the far end of the forest road, beside the woodcutter's crossing and within earshot of his work trail.
locations.mood: Comforting in its familiar details but increasingly claustrophobic once the wolf enters and alters the room.

props.name: Food Basket
props.description: A round woven basket lined with blue cloth and packed with bread, vegetable broth, soft cheese, apples, and a small jar of honey.
props.purpose: The gift for Grandmother, the practical reason for Red's journey, and the object the wolf intends to steal.
props.notes: The food arrangement should remain consistent. The blue cloth should remain visible beneath the lid, and the honey jar should never appear broken or opened.

props.name: Red Hooded Cloak
props.description: A hand-sewn scarlet wool cloak with a deep hood, a simple wooden clasp, and slight wear along the hem.
props.purpose: The protagonist's defining visual silhouette and a saturated color anchor against the muted forest.
props.notes: The hood is up outdoors, lowered inside each home.

props.name: Grandmother's Bonnet
props.description: A pale linen sleeping bonnet with a narrow lace edge and long ties.
props.purpose: A familiar object misused by the wolf as part of his unconvincing disguise.
props.notes: The bonnet should sit awkwardly over the wolf's ears so the audience can read the deception before Red fully accepts it.

props.name: Woodsman's Axe
props.description: A practical long-handled wood axe with a polished steel head and a worn ash grip.
props.purpose: Identifies the Woodsman's trade and gives him a credible way to hold the wolf at a distance without showing graphic violence.
props.notes: The blade is never used on screen. The Woodsman keeps the axe lowered after the wolf retreats.

organizations.name: Woodland Wardens
organizations.description: A small informal guild of foresters who maintain the public road, watch for storm damage and dangerous animals, and assist travelers between the village and outlying homes.
organizations.goals: Keep the forest road passable, respond to danger, and help isolated residents remain connected to the village.

episodes.title: The Road Through the Woods
episodes.synopsis: Little Red Riding Hood sets out with food for her sick grandmother, carelessly tells a courteous wolf where she is going, discovers his disguise at the cottage, and survives his attack with help from a nearby Woodsman. She returns home wiser about the difference between friendliness and trust.

scenes.title: A Promise and a Basket
scenes.summary: Red prepares a basket for her sick grandmother and leaves the safety of home with a clear purpose.
scenes.script_content:
INT. RED'S KITCHEN - MORNING

Morning light warms a small kitchen. LITTLE RED RIDING HOOD folds a blue cloth over bread, broth, cheese, apples, and honey. She checks each item, closes the basket, and fastens her scarlet cloak.

At the door, she looks toward the distant tree line. The errand is familiar, but this is the first time the responsibility belongs entirely to her. She lifts the basket and steps onto the road.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Grandmother needs something warm, something sweet, and a friendly face.
dialogue.description: Checking the basket contents with quiet determination.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: I'll be there before the afternoon shadows reach her gate.
dialogue.description: Fastening her cloak and taking responsibility for the journey.

scenes.production_notes: Begin with golden practical light and close tactile details of food, cloth, and basket weave. Preserve the packed-basket continuity established here.

scenes.title: The Stranger on the Forest Road
scenes.summary: A polite wolf draws Red into conversation, learns her destination, and secretly chooses a faster route to the cottage.
scenes.script_content:
EXT. DARK FOREST ROAD - LATE MORNING

Red follows the road beneath high branches. Birdsong thins as a GRAY WOLF steps from the ferns, careful to remain several paces away. He bows as though they are neighbors meeting in the village square.

Flattered by his manners, Red answers his questions and points toward the bend beyond which her grandmother lives. The wolf smiles, suggests that she gather a few cheerful flowers, then disappears along a narrow animal track.

Red watches the leaves settle behind him. A small doubt crosses her face, but she continues on the public road.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: Good morning, traveler. That basket looks far too important for an ordinary walk.
dialogue.description: Smoothly, from a respectful-looking distance.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: It's a basket of delicious treats for my grandmother. She's ill, and her cottage is just past the old oak at the far end of the road.
dialogue.description: Proud of her useful errand and unaware she has revealed too much.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: Then she is fortunate to have such a thoughtful granddaughter.
dialogue.description: Hiding his interest behind a courteous smile.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: The late flowers beside the creek would brighten her room.
dialogue.description: Indicating a harmless-looking detour while judging the shortcut.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Perhaps another day. I promised to arrive before the shadows grow long.
dialogue.description: Choosing the road, though still speaking more freely than she should.

scenes.emotional_tone: Courteous on the surface, with quiet predatory tension underneath.
scenes.production_notes: Keep a visible distance between Red and the wolf. Shift from natural birdsong to sparse forest ambience as his questions become more specific.

scenes.title: The Wolf Reaches the Cottage
scenes.summary: Taking a shortcut, the wolf arrives first, traps Grandmother safely in the pantry, and builds a hurried disguise.
scenes.script_content:
INT. GRANDMOTHER'S COTTAGE - MIDDAY

The wolf knocks softly and imitates Red's voice. GRANDMOTHER opens the door only a crack, but he shoulders inside. She backs toward the pantry, keeping a chair between them.

The wolf wants the food still coming down the road, not a noisy struggle. He forces Grandmother into the pantry and drops the heavy latch. Her pounding is muffled by the thick door.

In the bedroom, he pulls the curtains, puts on Grandmother's bonnet and shawl, and climbs beneath the patchwork quilt. His ears bend the bonnet out of shape. The cottage clock ticks while he practices a fragile voice.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: Grandmother, it's me. I've brought your basket.
dialogue.description: Imitating Red through the closed door.

dialogue.speaker: Grandmother
dialogue.line: That is not my granddaughter's step.
dialogue.description: Opening the door cautiously and recognizing danger too late.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: Be still, and this will be over as soon as the basket arrives.
dialogue.description: Low and impatient as he secures the pantry latch.

dialogue.speaker: Grandmother
dialogue.line: She will see through you.
dialogue.description: Firmly, from behind the pantry door.

scenes.emotional_tone: Urgent, confined, and suspenseful without graphic violence.
scenes.production_notes: Stage Grandmother's confinement clearly but gently: no injury is shown. The pantry latch must remain visible so the later rescue action reads instantly.

scenes.title: Eyes, Ears, and Teeth
scenes.summary: Red notices that the figure in Grandmother's bed is wrong; the wolf reveals himself, but a nearby Woodsman hears the commotion and drives him away.
scenes.script_content:
INT. GRANDMOTHER'S COTTAGE - AFTERNOON

Red enters, sets the basket on a stool, and approaches the darkened bed. The bonnet is familiar, but everything beneath it is the wrong shape. She studies the large ears, amber eyes, and long teeth as her questions become tests rather than innocent observations.

The wolf abandons the disguise and springs from the bed. Red pulls the stool between them and shouts. From the woodcutter's trail, the WOODSMAN hears furniture scrape and the pantry door shake. He rushes inside, steps between Red and the wolf, and raises his axe only as a barrier.

Outmatched and exposed, the wolf bolts through the open door and disappears into the forest. The Woodsman lowers the axe. Red immediately lifts the pantry latch and embraces Grandmother.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Grandmother, what large ears you have today.
dialogue.description: Keeping her voice even while she studies the misshapen bonnet.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: All the better to hear you with, my dear.
dialogue.description: Forcing a weak imitation of Grandmother's voice.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: And what bright eyes you have.
dialogue.description: Stepping back toward the stool and the open door.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: All the better to see you with.
dialogue.description: Letting his real voice break through.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Those are not Grandmother's teeth.
dialogue.description: Certain now, bracing the stool between them.

dialogue.speaker: The Wolf
dialogue.line: No. They are mine.
dialogue.description: Throwing off the quilt and revealing himself.

dialogue.speaker: The Woodsman
dialogue.line: Away from them. Back to the forest, now.
dialogue.description: Entering with controlled force and blocking the wolf's path to Red.

dialogue.speaker: Grandmother
dialogue.line: You noticed the truth before fear could silence you.
dialogue.description: After Red opens the pantry and helps her sit.

scenes.emotional_tone: Suspicion tightening into danger, then decisive relief.
scenes.production_notes: Build suspicion through eyelines and inserts before revealing the wolf. Choreograph the attack as a brief blocked advance: the stool and Woodsman maintain distance, and the axe is never swung.

scenes.title: The Safer Road Home
scenes.summary: After Grandmother is safe, the Woodsman escorts Red home, where she reflects on what trust should require.
scenes.script_content:
INT. RED'S KITCHEN - EVENING

The scarlet cloak lies folded beside the now-empty basket. Through the window, the Woodsman checks the road before continuing back toward the village.

Red sets a written note from Grandmother on the shelf and looks toward the dark tree line. The forest has not become evil, and kindness has not become foolish. What has changed is her understanding: a stranger earns trust through more than pleasant words. She closes the shutters, safe at home and better prepared for her next journey.

dialogue.speaker: The Woodsman
dialogue.line: A careful question can be as useful as a loud warning.
dialogue.description: At the doorway after escorting Red home.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: I'll still be kind. I just won't give my trust away before it has been earned.
dialogue.description: With calm conviction, setting down the empty basket.

scenes.production_notes: Echo the opening kitchen compositions with cooler evening light. End on Red closing the shutters without suggesting that she has become fearful of the world.

shots.title: Morning Kitchen Establishing Shot
shots.description: A slow push through the warm kitchen toward Red arranging food at the central table.
shots.editorial_notes: Open from black on the hearth glow, then reveal Red and the basket in the same frame.

shots.title: Basket Packing Inserts
shots.description: Tactile inserts of bread, broth, cheese, apples, honey, and the blue lining as Red checks each item.
shots.editorial_notes: Cut on hand movements and retain a final clean frame of the closed basket.

shots.title: Red Leaves Home
shots.description: Red fastens her cloak in profile, lifts the basket, and exits toward the distant forest road.
shots.editorial_notes: Match the red cloak's movement to the first exterior shot.

shots.title: Forest Road Establishing Shot
shots.description: Red appears small beneath the canopy as the road curves into deep shadow and the wolf watches unseen from the ferns.
shots.editorial_notes: Hold long enough for the audience to discover the wolf before he moves.

shots.title: The Courteous Encounter
shots.description: A measured two-shot preserves the space between Red and the wolf while his questions gradually direct her gaze toward the cottage road.
shots.editorial_notes: Let the blocking remain polite; tension comes from the wolf's attention to the basket and Red's pointing hand.

shots.title: The Wolf Chooses the Shortcut
shots.description: The wolf's courteous expression empties as he glances toward a narrow track and vanishes through foreground leaves.
shots.editorial_notes: Use the leaf wipe to transition from Red's road to the cottage door.

shots.title: A Knock at the Cottage
shots.description: From inside the quiet cottage, Grandmother approaches the door as the wolf's shadow crosses the frosted window.
shots.editorial_notes: Keep the pantry and bedroom doorways legible in the establishing composition.

shots.title: The Pantry Latch
shots.description: Grandmother backs into the pantry while keeping a chair between herself and the wolf; he closes the door and drops the latch.
shots.editorial_notes: Avoid impact imagery. End on Grandmother's hand visible at the safe gap beneath the door.

shots.title: An Unconvincing Disguise
shots.description: The wolf adjusts the lace bonnet around his ears, pulls the quilt up to his muzzle, and practices a fragile smile.
shots.editorial_notes: Balance menace with storybook absurdity; finish on the amber eyes opening.

shots.title: Red Enters the Darkened Room
shots.description: Red sets the basket on a stool and crosses toward the bed while the pantry door trembles almost imperceptibly behind her.
shots.editorial_notes: Use a deep composition so the bed, Red, basket, and pantry clue remain connected.

shots.title: Eyes, Ears, and Teeth
shots.description: Alternating close views trace Red's gaze from the misshapen ears to the amber eyes and finally the visible teeth as she backs toward the stool.
shots.editorial_notes: Shorten each response beat so the rhythm accelerates toward the reveal.

shots.title: Reveal and Rescue
shots.description: The wolf throws off the quilt and advances, Red blocks him with the stool, and the Woodsman enters to drive him through the open door before Red frees Grandmother.
shots.editorial_notes: Keep the geography simple and the action readable. Cut away from the fleeing wolf to the pantry latch opening.

shots.title: Escort at Dusk
shots.description: Seen through the kitchen window, Red and the Woodsman arrive from the forest road as the last daylight fades.
shots.editorial_notes: Mirror the opening palette while shifting the sky from gold to deep blue.

shots.title: Cloak and Empty Basket
shots.description: Red folds her cloak beside the empty basket and places Grandmother's note safely on the shelf.
shots.editorial_notes: Echo the packing inserts, but use fewer cuts and a calmer tempo.

shots.title: The Shutters Close
shots.description: After saying goodnight to the Woodsman, Red looks once toward the forest and closes the shutters with a thoughtful, steady expression.
shots.editorial_notes: Hold on the warm interior after the shutters meet, then fade out.

sounds.title: Morning Kitchen Ambience
sounds.description: Low hearth crackle, a kettle beginning to simmer, quiet crockery, and distant village birds.
sounds.production_notes: Keep the room intimate and natural; leave space for dialogue and detailed basket foley.

sounds.title: Opening Narration
sounds.description: A brief storybook narration establishes Grandmother's illness and Red's errand without duplicating the Scene dialogue.
sounds.spoken_text: Beyond the village and down the forest road, Grandmother was ill. Little Red Riding Hood packed what comfort she could carry and promised herself she would arrive before the shadows grew long.
sounds.production_notes: Warm adult storyteller voice, intimate rather than grand, recorded close with very little room tone.

sounds.title: Forest Road Ambience
sounds.description: Layered wind in pine needles, oak leaves, distant birds, insects, and occasional branch creaks that thin as the wolf approaches.
sounds.production_notes: Build from the linked sound-suite asset. Reduce the upper-canopy birds by half during the wolf's questions.

sounds.title: Hidden Step in the Ferns
sounds.description: One crisp twig break followed by soft leaves shifting as the wolf steps onto the road.
sounds.production_notes: Place slightly behind Red in the surround field so her turn feels motivated.

sounds.title: The Shortcut Motif
sounds.description: A restrained three-note low-string motif enters when the wolf drops his friendly expression and chooses the shortcut.
sounds.production_notes: Use dry cello harmonics and a soft frame-drum pulse; resolve into the cottage clock rhythm.

sounds.title: Cottage Clock and Quiet Room
sounds.description: An old clock ticks in a still cottage, with a faint stove draft and fabric movement.
sounds.production_notes: Let the clock become subjectively louder after the pantry latch drops.

sounds.title: Pantry Latch Drop
sounds.description: A heavy wooden door closes, followed by the decisive metal scrape and knock of the latch settling into place.
sounds.production_notes: Emphasize weight rather than volume; carry a shortened version into the later unlatching sound.

sounds.title: The Bonnet Falls
sounds.description: The shortcut motif returns with bowed bass, scraped wood, and a single drum accent as the wolf throws off the disguise.
sounds.production_notes: Peak on the reveal, then drop out before the Woodsman's command so his voice lands cleanly.

sounds.title: Stool, Boots, and Open Door
sounds.description: A stool scrapes across the floor, the Woodsman's boots cross the threshold, the axe handle knocks the doorframe, and the wolf's paws retreat into leaves.
sounds.production_notes: Keep each source distinct enough to tell the rescue through sound without implying an axe strike.

sounds.title: Closing Narration
sounds.description: The final narration frames Red's experience as discernment rather than fear.
sounds.spoken_text: Little Red Riding Hood returned home still kind, still brave, and much more careful. She had learned that friendly words can open a conversation, but only honest actions should open the door to trust.
sounds.production_notes: Use the opening narrator with a quieter, resolved delivery over the final two shots.

assets.title: Little Red Riding Hood Character Concept
assets.prompt: Full-body family-friendly storybook character design for Little Red Riding Hood, about twelve years old, vivid scarlet wool hooded cloak, cream blouse, dark skirt, sturdy walking shoes, woven basket, observant expression, autumn fairy-tale realism, front three-quarter and profile views.

assets.title: The Wolf Character Concept
assets.prompt: Large gray fairy-tale wolf with silver-tipped fur, amber eyes, expressive brows, long ears, powerful paws, capable of polite charm and sudden menace, family-friendly storybook realism, character turnaround with facial expression studies.

assets.title: Dark Forest Road Environment Concept
assets.prompt: Cinematic storybook forest road in autumn, ancient oaks and tall pines, dense ferns, shafts of cool light, russet leaves, narrow dirt path bending into shadow, beautiful but watchful mood, no characters, 16:9 composition.

assets.title: Grandmother's Cottage Interior Concept
assets.prompt: Small fairy-tale cottage interior with patchwork bed, iron stove, old clock, herb bundles, heavy-latched pantry, low windows and creaking front door, warm handmade textures made suspenseful by drawn curtains, family-friendly cinematic storybook style, 16:9.

assets.title: Food Basket Prop Concept
assets.prompt: Round handwoven willow basket with hinged lid and blue linen lining, neatly packed bread, covered broth jar, soft cheese, red apples and small honey jar, practical fairy-tale film prop, neutral turnaround lighting.

assets.title: Forest Ambience and Story Motif Suite
assets.prompt: Create separated production stems for an autumn forest ambience and a restrained three-note suspense motif using cello harmonics, soft frame drum, bowed bass, leaves, distant birds and branch creaks. Family-friendly, intimate, naturalistic, and suitable beneath dialogue.

editorial_artifacts.title: Little Red Riding Hood Master Shot List
editorial_artifacts.notes: Development shot list covering the full five-scene short. Scene 4, Shot 12 is the key safety and choreography review shot because it contains the reveal, blocked attack, Woodsman's entrance, wolf's retreat, and pantry rescue.
